title: Provisional measurement review
notice: These are newly derived, unvalidated educational observations. The source supplies no printed answer key for this exercise. They are unscored and require qualified ECG educator review.

fields.basis: Visually checked ventricular landmarks on original PDF 526
fields.reason: Successive ventricular peak spacings: 134 px, 122 px, 173 px, 172 px. Descriptive judgment from visible spacing, not a validated diagnostic threshold.

fields.basis: Course-standard 25 mm/s assumption; 150 independently detected small-square intervals across 738 pixels
fields.reason: Mean R–R estimate 49.1 bpm; six-second count estimate 50 bpm. All seconds/bpm depend on course-standard 25 mm/s. Count estimate assumes 150 small squares = 6 seconds; endpoint phase and partial complexes affect it. On irregular strips the count estimate is not a stable instantaneous rate. Mean RR describes only intervals between observed peaks.

fields.value: Candidate P-wave observation: Very low rounded pre-complex bumps recur on an otherwise nearly flat baseline. They are much smaller than the later broad waves and only modestly larger than raster/baseline thickness.
fields.basis: Original PDF page 526; independently reconciled selected-complex observation
fields.reason: Provisional deflection description, not validated atrial identity or a diagnosis. Describes visible morphology/association only, not established P identity, atrial origin or conduction. Are the tiny bumps atrial P waves or baseline texture, and should the small initial negative dip be included in QRS? This describes only the selected complexes or restricted subset. It does not establish a whole-strip event census, ventricular sequence completeness, atrial identity, or conduction relationship. Qualified ECG educator review is outstanding.

fields.basis: Original PDF page 526; independently reconciled endpoint bands and horizontal grid; assumes course 25 mm/s (0.04 s per small square), not a verified per-strip speed
fields.reason: Propose broad conditional QRS envelope: small initial negative dip, sharp positive complex and bounded decay to a stable shelf can be separated from the later broad wave. Assumes course 25 mm/s and correct component identity/boundaries. Envelopes describe measurement uncertainty, not actual duration variability. Are the tiny bumps atrial P waves or baseline texture, and should the small initial negative dip be included in QRS? This describes only the selected complexes or restricted subset. It does not establish a whole-strip event census, ventricular sequence completeness, atrial identity, or conduction relationship. This envelope includes reader and endpoint uncertainty; it is not a confidence interval, normal/abnormal classification, or proof of beat-to-beat physiological variation. Qualified ECG educator review is outstanding.

limitations: Wave observations and conditional endpoint envelopes remain provisional and unscored. QT/QTc, calibrated amplitudes and clinical diagnosis are not established. Selected-complex widths do not establish sequence certainty.

P-wave text is a provisional description, not validated atrial identity. PR remains unresolved with no numerical answer. QRS has an unvalidated conditional endpoint envelope for selected complexes. Validated electrical boundaries and qualified educator adjudication remain outstanding.
Calibration assumes the course’s 25 mm/s convention, not speed metadata printed on each strip. Peak uncertainty is approximately ±2 source pixels, excluding errors in identifying the waveform.
